first_impression.reaction: The intro didn't open with the usual 'fairytale garden' gush. It went straight to the trade-off, which made me keep going: 'the garden that sets the mood is also the venue with the least shelter from the weather.' That's the honest bit we never get from venue brochures. I skimmed the real weddings, then actually read the venue questions, because that's where it got useful.

journey.quote: It works when the styling and the backup plan are decided together, because the garden that sets the mood is also the venue with the least shelter from the weather.
journey.reaction: Good. An honest trade-off in the second sentence. That earns the skim turning into a read.

journey.section: Real garden weddings from our pages
journey.quote: Eight couples and eight gardens, each described as their own story tells it.
journey.reaction: Nice that they're your own couples, but none of the eight has a date and most don't say where they were. I can't tell what month the Adelaide one was, or which of these were abroad apart from Dubai. Real weddings with a venue and date are what I'd send to my mum.

journey.section: Real garden weddings from our pages
journey.quote: The gardens gave their guests a warm, romantic space to spend it in.
journey.reaction: This one line is filler. It could be about any garden anywhere. The others at least say something you could picture.

journey.quote: Put the front rows, and the grandparents, where the shade falls at the hour of the ceremony, with every row on level ground.
journey.reaction: This is exactly our worry. Someone who's actually stood on a lawn at 3pm wrote this. I'd forward this bit to James's mum.

journey.quote: Design the lighting for the hour your reception ends, not the hour it begins.
journey.reaction: Simple, practical, and not something I'd have thought of. Insider-ish.

journey.section: What to plan for with your venue
journey.quote: Each point below ends in questions to ask before you book, and the answers belong in writing.
journey.reaction: As a lawyer, yes. This is the most useful part of the page. A checklist I could actually take into a site visit.

journey.section: Wet weather plan and covered space
journey.quote: Who makes the call to move under cover, and by what time on the day?
journey.reaction: The accountability question. This is the thing that goes wrong on the day and nobody owns it. Glad it's asked.

journey.quote: Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before going outside and again every two hours, so set a sunscreen station out well before guests take their seats.
journey.reaction: Fine, but the sun-safety part runs a bit long. We know about SunSmart. The sunscreen station is the only line here that's actually a wedding idea.

journey.section: Access for older guests and a route without steps
journey.quote: Walk the day as your oldest guest would.
journey.reaction: Love this. One line, and it says the whole thing.

journey.quote: How do guests travel between the hotel and the garden, and how long does it take?
journey.reaction: Half our guests are flying in, so this is the section that matters to us most. It's good, but it's only five bullets after a long Australian section. I wanted more of this and less sunscreen.

journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Quoting in AUD speaks straight to our currency worry, and 'in writing' speaks to the hidden-costs one. This is the line that made me take the brand seriously.

journey.section: Plan your garden wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: A single point of contact is what we want. But every planner says start to finish. It doesn't tell me who is physically there on the day, or whether the vendors are people you know or strangers you've found online. And still no idea what the fee looks like, even roughly.

unanswered_questions: When and where were these eight weddings? I'd like a month and a place for each, at least for the ones that were abroad.
Does our Wedded Advisor, or someone from Wedded Wonderland, attend on the day, or is the venue's coordinator the person on the ground?
If something goes wrong on the day, who is accountable: you, the venue or the vendor?
Are the vendors people you've worked with before, or sourced fresh for each wedding?
What does the Concierge fee roughly look like? Even a range or how it's worked out would help.
Do you have garden venues abroad that you'd recommend for a group of 60 to 90 with older guests?

turn_offs_found.quote: The gardens gave their guests a warm, romantic space to spend it in.
turn_offs_found.why: Generic wedding-blog filler. Not a cliché on my banned list, but in the same family.

turn_offs_found.quote: A garden is the loveliest setting to get right and the easiest to leave to chance.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Loveliest' is a bit soft and sales-y after a page that was refreshingly practical. The second half is the point; the first half isn't needed.

turn_offs_found.quote: the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: Better than nothing, but it's still vague pricing with no range. In writing is reassuring; no idea of scale is not.

would_share_with: James (the venue questions section, as a checklist)
Our parents (the seating and access for older guests parts)

cta_reaction.quote: Tell Wedded Concierge the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming.
cta_reaction.why: It's low-key, not a hard sell, and 'Bring this list to your first conversation' is a nice touch. But we're 14 months out with no destination, and this is the first post of yours we've read. I'd bookmark it and read a couple more, plus a real wedding with a venue and a date, before filling anything in.

The gardens gave their guests a warm, romantic space to spend it in." NEW: "[Kristyn and Damien](/real-wedding-an-elegant-garden-wedding-in-adelaide) married in a garden in Adelaide and went from their ceremony straight into a cocktail party in the gardens."

Add the accountability question to the destination list, as a question only. OLD: "- Who is on the venue's side on the day, and do they stay until the end of the night?" NEW: "- Who is on the venue's side on the day, and do they stay until the end of the night?
- If something goes wrong on the day, who answers for it, and how do you reach them?"

Drop the soft opener in the closing section. OLD: "A garden is the loveliest setting to get right and the easiest to leave to chance." NEW: "A garden asks more of the planning than any room, and every answer above needs an owner."

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (planner_couple), judging only what matters to them
No invented brand facts; missing information listed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings adding no prices, venue or vendor names, statistics, business details or new facts about the real weddings
Scores are 1 to 5 and top_3_changes has at most 3 items

assumptions: Arrival context was not specified; read as if arriving from a Google search for 'garden wedding' during early research.
Persona is provisional (not CRM-calibrated), so reactions reflect the assumed profile.
URL slugs in links are not visible to the reader and were not judged as copy.

open_questions.question: Can the real wedding cards show a month or location per wedding where the source stories publish them? This persona trusts real weddings with venue and date.
Can the closing section state, from an approved brand source, whether a Wedded Advisor or team member is present on the day? It is this persona's main remaining objection.
